metadata.title: Can AI Predict Your Next Click? — How Customer Engagement Scoring Works
alternative_titles: Click. Convert. Leave. — How AI Predicts Customer Behavior
Predictive Customer Analytics — How AI Scores Engagement
metadata.central_question: Can AI really predict what a customer will do next?
metadata.answer: It estimates probabilities from past behavior — prediction is not certainty.
metadata.framework: EVENTS → FEATURES → MODEL → PROBABILITY → ACTION → MEASURE
metadata.demo_brand: BrewBox — a fictional online coffee shop. All customers and events are synthetic (seed 20260912).
metadata.clock: measured Kokoro af_kore narration — the master clock

beats.title: Presenter intro
beats.narration: Hi, I am Dhrumil Shah, and this video is about how AI estimates which customers will click, buy, or leave, and why those scores are probabilities, not certainties.
beats.visual_intent: Presenter introduces himself and states the one-sentence summary before the cold open.
beats.scene_description: Large serif greeting 'Hi, I'm Dhrumil Shah.' A summary card fades in on 'this video is about'; click / buy / leave chips pop with the spoken words; the six-stage pipeline previews underneath.
on_screen_text: How AI estimates who will click, buy, or leave — and why a score is a probability, not a certainty.
EVENTS → FEATURES → MODEL → PROBABILITY → ACTION → MEASURE
beats.animation: Greeting spring-in; summary card reveals on 'this video is about'; chips pop on their spoken words; pipeline chips stagger in.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Greeting y 300–520; summary card y 600–900; three behaviour chips y 940; pipeline preview y 1060–1300.

beats.title: Cold open — three customers, three scores
beats.narration: Five thousand coffee-shop customers. Will this one click? Will this one buy? Is this one about to leave? A model answers: eighty-nine, seventy, sixty-eight percent. But how does it know?
beats.visual_intent: Create curiosity in the first three seconds: a crowd becomes three individuals, each with a real model probability, then the claim is interrupted.
beats.scene_description: Hundreds of customer nodes pour into a grid. Three nodes enlarge into cards A/B/C with probability rings (CLICK 89%, BUY 70%, LEAVE 68%). The rings freeze; a terracotta question 'But how does it know?' slams in.
beats.animation: Node grid staggered spring-in (0–1.2s); three nodes scale up and slide into stacked cards (1.2–3s); rings count up; question slams at the 'how' word.
beats.chart_data: video_data.json#/hook (customers C02661, C01211, C04293 on test date 2026-07-04)
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Top: small kicker 'BREWBOX · 5,000 SYNTHETIC CUSTOMERS'. Middle: dot grid 900×620 with three stacked customer cards. Lower-middle: question line. Nothing below y 1360 except captions.

beats.title: The honest answer
beats.narration: It doesn't know. It estimates probabilities from past behavior.
beats.visual_intent: Replace certainty with probability before any mechanism is shown.
beats.scene_description: Large serif 'It doesn't know.' A 0–100% probability bar fills to a marker; the marker is fuzzy (uncertainty band). Chip: PREDICTION ≠ CERTAINTY.
beats.animation: Headline type-in; bar fill with soft uncertainty band; chip pops.
beats.transition: pipeline tracker slides down from the top
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Headline at y 360; probability bar centred at y 820; chip at y 1080.

beats.title: Events
beats.narration: It starts with events: emails, clicks, visits, product views, carts, purchases, each with a customer ID and a timestamp.
beats.visual_intent: Show that a model begins with logged data, not intuition.
beats.scene_description: Vertical event log for Customer C02661: real timestamped rows (from the event table) stack downward with type icons; particles flow into a counter '1,217,852 events'.
beats.animation: Rows drop in one per 0.4s with a tick; particles stream to the counter.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Pipeline tracker at top (EVENTS lit). Event rows full-width 900px, y 420–1180. Counter below.

beats.title: Raw events become features
beats.narration: Events become features, counted only before the prediction date. Visits in thirty days. Purchases in ninety. Days since last activity.
beats.visual_intent: Make feature engineering and the point-in-time boundary visible.
beats.scene_description: A vertical time axis with a terracotta PREDICTION DATE line. Events above the line (PAST) collapse into a feature vector card; the area below (FUTURE) is hatched and locked.
beats.animation: Event dots slide into bins; values count up; lock icon on the future strip.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: PAST block y 360–760, prediction line y 800, feature vector card y 860–1300, FUTURE hatched strip hint beside the line.

beats.title: Define the target
beats.narration: Then define the target. Click within seven days? Buy within seven? Churn, in this demo, means thirty days with no click, visit, or purchase. Real businesses define it differently.
beats.visual_intent: A model needs an explicit yes/no question with a window; churn must be defined, not implied.
beats.scene_description: Three stacked target cards — MODEL A CLICK · 7 DAYS, MODEL B BUY · 7 DAYS, MODEL C CHURN · 30 DAYS — each with a 0 / 1 toggle and a window bar. Footnote plate: demo definition.
on_screen_text: MODEL C · Churn = no click, visit or purchase for 30 days → 0 / 1
DEMO DEFINITION — real businesses define churn differently
beats.animation: Cards slide in; window bars sweep; 0/1 toggles flick.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Cards full width at y 420, 700, 980; footnote at y 1270.

beats.title: Training on the past, testing on the later month
beats.narration: Training pairs past features with what happened next. Earlier months train the model. A later month it never saw tests it, so the future can't leak in.
beats.visual_intent: Training = features compared with known outcomes; chronological split prevents leakage.
beats.scene_description: A vertical calendar of prediction dates: Mar 21, Apr 5, Apr 20 (TRAIN), May 20 (VALIDATE), Jul 4 (TEST). Rows of features + actual outcome flow into a logistic-regression block; a short real code excerpt appears.
beats.animation: Rows stream through model; weights bars settle; TEST block unlocks last.
beats.transition: test block zooms into Customer A card
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Calendar spine left-centre y 360–1000; model block right; code card y 1060–1320.

beats.title: Customer A
beats.narration: Customer A: twenty-two visits this month, ten purchases in ninety days, active yesterday.
beats.visual_intent: Ground the model in one concrete, recently active customer.
beats.scene_description: Customer card C02661 with four feature rows and sparkline of visits; feature vector feeds a model block.
beats.animation: Values count up in sync with narration.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Card centred y 380–1080; arrow into model chip at y 1180.

beats.title: Probabilities — and what actually happened
beats.narration: Click: eighty-nine percent. Buy: sixty-one. Churn risk: under one percent. That week, Customer A clicked, but didn't buy. A probability is not a promise.
beats.visual_intent: Show probabilities as outputs and reveal the real outcome to prove they are not certainties.
beats.scene_description: Three probability rings fill: CLICK 89%, BUY 61%, CHURN RISK <1%. Then outcome stamps: CLICKED ✓, BOUGHT ✗, STILL ACTIVE ✓.
on_screen_text: A probability is not a promise
beats.animation: Ring sweeps with score ticks; stamps land on 'clicked, but didn't buy'.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Rings stacked vertically y 360–1060 with labels left; outcome stamps to the right of each ring; caption line y 1180.

beats.title: Customer B — the contrast
beats.narration: Customer B: silent for seventy-four days. Click: two percent. Churn risk: seventy-three.
beats.visual_intent: Contrast makes the pattern intuitive: inactivity → low engagement probability, high churn risk.
beats.scene_description: Customer card C03887: event log shows only 'email sent' rows (no responses). Rings: CLICK 2%, BUY <1%, CHURN RISK 73%.
beats.animation: Send rows appear with no response ticks; churn ring fills terracotta.
beats.transition: both cards dissolve into the population
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Top half: muted event log of sends only; bottom half: three compact rings; warning state uses triangle icon + label, not colour alone.

beats.title: Segment the population
beats.narration: Scores rank everyone. The team sets cutoffs for high, medium, and at risk. Those are business choices, not laws of nature.
beats.visual_intent: Continuous scores become actionable groups via thresholds chosen by people.
beats.scene_description: 420 real customer points plotted by click probability (x) and churn risk (y); dashed cutoffs labelled BUSINESS CHOICE; points regroup into three shape-coded columns with counts.
on_screen_text: 623 lapsed customers sit outside the churn population
beats.animation: Points animate from scatter to clustered columns.
beats.transition: segment columns slide left into action rows
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Scatter 900×760 at y 360; three segment count cards below y 1150–1320.

beats.title: Marketing actions as tests, not verdicts
beats.narration: Each segment gets something to test: a new-roast email, an offer, a win-back message, or fewer emails. Consent and human review still apply.
beats.visual_intent: Predictions inform decisions; decisions stay governed.
beats.scene_description: Four rows: segment → suggested test. A guardrail bar runs across all rows: CONSENT · PRIVACY · HUMAN REVIEW · HOLDOUT.
beats.animation: Rows connect with arrows; guardrail slides over them.

beats.title: Does the model work?
beats.narration: Does it work? On the unseen month, customers scored near fifty-five percent bought at fifty-six percent. That's calibration.
beats.visual_intent: Show held-out evaluation and what a calibrated probability means.
beats.scene_description: Manim reliability diagram of the purchase model on the test month: 10 bins plotted against the diagonal; top bin highlighted 55% predicted vs 56% observed. Metric chips ROC-AUC 0.89 · PR-AUC 0.58 vs base 0.12.
beats.animation: Diagonal draws; bins pop in; top bin pulses.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Manim clip 936×936 in a card at y 330; metric chips y 1300.

beats.title: Prediction is not causation
beats.narration: But prediction isn't causation. A high scorer might have bought anyway. Only a holdout test shows whether the campaign caused anything.
beats.visual_intent: Separate predictive accuracy from causal impact.
beats.scene_description: Equation card: PREDICTED CONVERSION ≠ CAMPAIGN CAUSED CONVERSION. Below, an ILLUSTRATIVE holdout diagram: high scorers split into CAMPAIGN and HOLDOUT groups; the difference between them is labelled 'lift = the causal question'.
on_screen_text: ILLUSTRATIVE — no uplift experiment was run
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Equation y 380–640; holdout diagram y 720–1260; ILLUSTRATIVE plate top-right of diagram.

beats.title: Real platforms, noisy signals, bad data
beats.narration: Salesforce documents Einstein Engagement Scoring predicting opens, clicks, subscriber retention, and web conversion. But opens are noisy: Apple Mail can download email images in the background. And bad data makes confident, wrong scores.
beats.tts_text: Salesforce documents Einstein Engagement Scoring predicting opens, clicks, subscriber retention, and web conversion. But opens are noisy: Apple Mail can download email images in the background. And bad data makes confident, wrong scores.
beats.visual_intent: One concrete industry example, the open-tracking caveat, and the data-quality warning.
beats.scene_description: Card 1: SALESFORCE-DOCUMENTED — four predicted behaviours with source tag. Card 2: OPENS ARE NOISY — synthetic demo bars: pre-fetch mail clients logged 8.4 opens vs 3.4, with near-identical clicks 1.9 vs 1.8. Card 3: garbage-in warning.
on_screen_text: opens · clicks · subscriber retention · web conversion

beats.title: Where Claude fits — and who decides
beats.narration: Claude isn't the predictor here. It explains scores in plain language, flags leakage, and drafts the next experiment. People decide what's fair.
beats.visual_intent: Keep the predictive model and the Claude reasoning layer distinct; end with the human boundary.
beats.scene_description: Architecture stack: CUSTOMER DATA → PREDICTIVE MODEL (scikit-learn) → PROBABILITY SCORES → CLAUDE (explain · flag · draft) → HUMAN DECISION. Two columns below: AI/ML: SCORE · RANK · SEGMENT; TEAM: DECIDE · TEST · REVIEW.
on_screen_text: CLAUDE · explain · flag leakage · draft test
beats.animation: Stack builds top-down; Claude block glows terracotta; human block lands last.
beats.transition: stack rotates into the final pipeline
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Stack y 340–1000; two-column boundary card y 1060–1300.

beats.title: Ending — prediction is not certainty
beats.narration: So, can AI predict your next click? It turns past behavior into probabilities that people can test. Events. Features. Model. Probability. Action. Measure. Prediction is not certainty.
beats.visual_intent: Resolve the opening question and leave the full pipeline in memory.
beats.scene_description: The six pipeline stages light one by one on each spoken word, stacked vertically; then everything fades to a single end card: 'Prediction ≠ Certainty'.
beats.animation: Stages light in sync with the six spoken words; final fade to end card during end hold.
beats.composition_9x16_source_cut: Six stage blocks y 380–1240; end card centred.
